newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tobacco industry says price cutting only option.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco industry says price cutting only option.

text.p: European Union tobacco manufacturers, retailers and workers on Monday vigorously rejected criticism by the European Union's top health official, saying that price cutting was the only way to raise sales.
On Friday, EU Health Commissioner Padraig Flynn condemned a new cigarette price war as a ploy to attract new smokers and get round advertising bans.
"Flynn has declared war on the tobacco industry," said Robert Toet, Chairman of the Confederation of European Community Cigarette Manufacturers.
"There are some who want to destroy the tobacco industry," he added in a statement, noting attempts to stop tobacco companies sponsoring sports events and to abolish subsidies for tobacco farmers.

Speaking at a news conference to launch a study showing that the tobacco industry was a major provider of jobs and tax revenue, Toet said price cutting was the only means left for companies to compete for sales.
Remy Tritschler, President of the European Confederation of Tobacco Retailers (CEDT), said the cigarette trade should be allowed some marketing flexibility.
"The price war is awful and very difficult to bear," the Frenchman said in a passionate attack on the anti-smoking lobby.
"Smoking is a pleasure and demand will continue," he added.
More than 95 million people, or a third of all adults, smoke in the European Union.

The tobacco industry study, published by Pieda Plc, showed that 1.42 million people work in the tobacco industry, mostly in Greece and Italy, generating some 51 billion ecus ($58 billion) of tax revenue. Nearly 75 per cent of the cost of a cigarette is tax.
"The economic aspects should be taken into account," said Donald MacKay, Pieda Chairman, claiming that revenue from excise duty and VAT on tobacco products was far greater than resulting costs.
Cigarette firms complain that the EU's executive has focused attention on the health aspects and failed to take an overall view.

In a statement to mark World No-Tobacco Day on Saturday, Flynn said that 30 percent of all cancers were tobacco related, smoking caused three million deaths a year worldwide and six major studies had concluded passive smoking increased the risk of lung cancer, heart disease and childhood asthma.
The Irish commissioner's criticism of the price war, his fourth direct attack on tobacco companies in the last two years, will be put to EU health ministers on June 5.
Tobacco manufacturers shrugged off plans by Britain's new Labour government for a national ban on tobacco ads and sponsorship of sports events.
Toet said that British plans were still at an early stage and would not end resistance from a blocking minority of EU governments.
